concepts.title: Count of Multiples up to a Limit

questions.q: Evaluate the limit of 1x^2 + 5x + 7 as x approaches 4 (direct substitution).
By the power rule, the derivative of 3x^3 is 9x^2. Find the derivative's value at x = 4.
For y = 4x^2 + 4x + 1, find the slope of the tangent at x = 1.
For y = 4x^2 + 4x + 1 at x = 1, the tangent slope is m; find the slope of the normal (-1/m), two decimal places.
Chain rule: y = (5x + 2)^3 has dy/dx = 15(5x + 2)^2. Evaluate it at x = 2.
Second derivative test: for y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2, y'' = 6x - 6. Evaluate y'' at the critical point x = 1 to classify it.
Two numbers 30 and 40 have HCF 10 with coprime multipliers 3 and 4. Verify by computing hcf = 10 x 1; then find the HCF value.
Find the LCM of 30 and 40 given their HCF is 10 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 30 and 40 is 120. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 30 cm and 40 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 30 minutes and 40 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 18 are there up to 96?

solution_steps.action: use the prime-factor / HCF-LCM relation for the two numbers
solution_steps.explain: use the prime-factor / HCF-LCM relation for the two numbers: hcf = 8 * 1 gives 8

questions.q: Two numbers 56 and 16 have HCF 8 with coprime multipliers 7 and 2. Verify by computing hcf = 8 x 1; then find the HCF value.
Find the LCM of 56 and 16 given their HCF is 8 and HCF x LCM = product of the numbers.
The LCM of 56 and 16 is 112. Use HCF x LCM = a x b to find their HCF.
Two ropes of lengths 56 cm and 16 cm are cut into equal pieces of greatest length. What is the length of each piece?
Two bells ring together now. They ring at intervals of 56 minutes and 16 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
How many multiples of 12 are there up to 120?

solution_steps.explain: verify the number-theory claim numerically: lhs = 3 ** 3 + 4 ** 3 gives 91
verify the number-theory claim numerically: diff = 5 ** 3 - lhs gives 34

questions.q: Fermat's Last Theorem says x^n + y^n = z^n has no positive solutions for n > 2. For n = 3 compute 5^3 - (3^3 + 4^3) to see it is not zero.
Check whether 6 is a perfect number: its proper divisors are 1, 2 and 3. Find their sum.
The numbers 11 and 13 are consecutive primes. How far apart are they (twin primes differ by 2)?
Are 8 and 15 co-prime? Their common factors are only 1, so their HCF is what?
Divisibility by 9: a number is divisible by 9 when its digit sum is. Find the digit sum of 729 and report the digit sum.
Divisibility by 11: add and subtract alternate digits of 2728 from the right (8 - 2 + 7 - 2) and report the result.

solution_steps.action: use the prime-factor / HCF-LCM relation for the two numbers
solution_steps.explain: use the prime-factor / HCF-LCM relation for the two numbers: hcf = 9 * 1 gives 9
